RagShortTexts: The ruling elite of Sarmatians comprised ancient aristocratic houses and military dynasties competing for feudal land and fiscal control.
Domestic politics were profoundly steered by court intrigues and noble factions resisting excessive central centralization.
Intricate matrimonial alliances and blood feuds permeated the nobility, ensuring that disputed successions frequently sparked nationwide crises.

Variants.Content: Within the opulent halls and sprawling feudal estates of Sarmatians, the balance of domestic power remained in perilous equilibrium. Ancient lineages commanded vast agricultural latifundia, hereditary warrior retinues, and lucrative trade monopolies, acting simultaneously as imperial cornerstones and covert rivals to the throne. Court assemblies seethed with venomous factionalism, pitting entrenched senatorial aristocrats against battle-hardened military commanders who demanded greater political dominance. Behind tapestried corridors, clandestine poisonings, forged wills, and intercepted treaties dictated political ascendancy. Lesser vassals maneuvered cautiously between dominant magnates, ready to shift allegiance whenever the central authority showed signs of exhaustion or military defeat.

Outside the chieftain's hall, the gate-riders stand stiff while voices rise inside. The chieftain's son and his brother-in-law have overturned a bronze cauldron, and the guards keep their eyes on the floor. When great clans quarrel over grazing rights, it is the common riders at the gate who take the first blows. At the Sarmatians post, the night watchword is "Storm."

Kumis cools in the bowl as the old elder counsels his heir. The chieftain's title matters less than the herds, the strongholds, and the households that owe service to them. Smile at the council and accept every toast, but keep a dagger under the cloak until the rival clan's pastures are yours.
